texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a master of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. Word has reached the guild of the {TALE} {A_nameDef} made, and {X_pronoun} asks to judge it where it is. If it is true work it gets the guild's mark. If {X_pronoun} finds a fault in it, {X_pronoun} will say so.

[legend] {X_nameDef}, a master of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. The guild has heard that {A_nameDef} made a legendary piece, the {TALE}, and {X_pronoun} would like to judge it where it is. A true piece gets the guild's mark. A fault in it would be said plainly.

[age0] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked to the gate with a carver's bag. Word of the {TALE} {A_nameDef} made has reached the guild's people, and {X_pronoun} asks to look it over. If it is good work the guild will mark it as such. If it hides a flaw, {X_pronoun} will say so.

[age1] {X_nameDef}, a master of {FACTION} in the guild's ochre apron, has come to the gate. The guild has heard of the {TALE} {A_nameDef} made, and {X_pronoun} would judge it as the guild judges its own work. True work gets the guild's mark. Bad work is called bad.

[age2] {X_nameDef}, a master of {FACTION}, has come up the road with a case of gauges and a lens. Word of the {TALE} {A_nameDef} made has reached the guild, and {X_pronoun} asks to test it where it is. If it holds up it gets the guild's mark, and if it doesn't, {X_pronoun} will say what is wrong with it.

[age3] {X_nameDef}, a master of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a scanner and a set of gauges. The guild has heard of the {TALE} {A_nameDef} made, and {X_pronoun} would like to check it over. A true piece gets the guild's mark. A hidden fault would be named.

[held] {X_nameDef}, a master of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. Word has reached the guild of the {TALE} {A_nameDef} made, and {X_pronoun} asks to look at it on {A_nameDef} where {A_pronoun} is. If it is true work it gets the guild's mark. If {X_pronoun} finds a fault, {X_pronoun} will say so.

li.label: Let {X_objective} judge the {TALE}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} will go to the {TALE} and look it over for an hour, with {A_nameDef} beside {X_objective}.

li.label: Let {X_objective} judge it, and go over it with {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} will look the {TALE} over with {A_nameDef}, and tell {A_objective} what {X_pronoun} sees in the work as {X_pronoun} goes.

li.label: We'll keep it to ourselves
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods and goes back to the road.

lines.li: [judge] Show me the work, and I'll tell you what it is.
[later] Then the guild will hear of it from others.
[true] This is true work, and the guild's mark goes on it.
[true] There's no lie in this one, it gets the mark.
[fault] There is a fault in this, and I won't put the mark on it.
[fault] Look here, the work goes wrong at this point.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has come back to the gate. A year ago {X_pronoun} spent {X_possessive} wander-year at {A_nameDef}'s bench. {X_pronoun} is a master of {FACTION} now, and has brought a {TALE} {X_pronoun} made as a gift for the colony.

[better] {X_nameDef}, who spent {X_possessive} wander-year at {A_nameDef}'s bench a year ago, has come back to the gate a master of {FACTION}. {X_pronoun} says the year at the colony taught {X_objective} more than any other, and has brought a {TALE} {X_pronoun} made as a gift.

[age0] {X_nameDef} has walked back to the gate a year after {X_possessive} wander-year at {A_nameDef}'s side. {FACTION} have made {X_objective} a master, and {X_pronoun} has carried a {TALE} {X_pronoun} made all the way here as a gift.

[age1] {X_nameDef} has come back to the gate wearing a master's apron of {FACTION}. A year ago {X_pronoun} worked at {A_nameDef}'s bench on {X_possessive} wander-year. {X_pronoun} has brought a {TALE} of {X_possessive} own making as a gift for the colony.

[age2] {X_nameDef} has come back up the road a year after {X_possessive} wander-year at {A_nameDef}'s bench, a master of {FACTION} now. {X_pronoun} has a {TALE} {X_pronoun} made in a crate on {X_possessive} back, as a gift for the colony.

[age3] {X_nameDef}, who did {X_possessive} wander-year at {A_nameDef}'s bench a year ago, has come back to the gate as a master of {FACTION}. {X_pronoun} has brought a {TALE} {X_pronoun} made as a gift for the colony.

li.label: Take the gift, and let {A_nameDef} sit with {X_objective} a while
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sets the {TALE} down at the gate, and {A_nameDef} sits with {X_objective} for an hour or so.

li.label: Take the gift, and have {X_objective} work a morning at the bench with {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sets the {TALE} down at the gate, and works beside {A_nameDef} for a few hours, showing {A_objective} what {X_pronoun} learned since.

li.label: Thank {X_objective} at the gate
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sets the {TALE} down at the gate and goes back to the road.

lines.li: [sit] I've a lot to tell you about the year.
[bench] Let me show you what I do differently now.
[gate] Keep it somewhere it will be looked at.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a journeyman of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. {X_pronoun} and two others would camp by the colony for a week or so and build {TALE}, with {COUNT} of the colony's {THING} from its stores. The work would be the colony's, with the guild's mark on it.

[bridge] {X_nameDef}, a journeyman of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. The guild's first master rebuilt a bridge three times and marked every stone, and the guild still builds bridges where it can. {X_pronoun} and two others would camp by the colony for a week or so and build {TALE}, with {COUNT} of the colony's {THING}.

[age0] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked to the gate with mallets and chisels in a bag. {X_pronoun} and two others would camp by the colony for some days and make {TALE}, from {COUNT} of the colony's {THING}. It would stay the colony's after they go.

[age1] {X_nameDef}, a journeyman of {FACTION} in the guild's ochre apron, has come to the gate. Three of the guild's journeymen would camp by the colony for a week or so and build {TALE}, with {COUNT} of the colony's {THING}, and cut the guild's mark into it.

[age2] {X_nameDef}, a journeyman of {FACTION}, has come up the road with a cart of tools. {X_pronoun} and two others would camp by the colony for a week or so and build {TALE}, from {COUNT} of the colony's {THING}. It would carry the guild's mark.

[age3] {X_nameDef}, a journeyman of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with cutting tools and a set of plans. Three journeymen would camp by the colony for a week or so and build {TALE}, from {COUNT} of the colony's {THING}, with the guild's mark on it.

li.label: Let them build it ({COUNT} {THING})
li.outcome: The three journeymen will camp by the colony. Once they have settled, the {THING} is carried out to them, and they start on the work.

li.label: Let them build it, and send {A_nameDef} to work beside them
li.outcome: The three journeymen will camp by the colony, and {A_nameDef} will work beside them during their working hours and learn.

li.label: Not now
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods and goes back to the road.

lines.li: [build] We'll make something here that lasts.
[later] Then another town will get the work.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an operator of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. The Line gives each place one call a season on its masts, and this season's is the colony's if it wants it, at the Line's price. It could call for a trader of goods or of arms, for hands, or put in a good word for the colony with a people it stands poorly with.

[radio] {X_nameDef}, an operator of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. The Line gives each place one call a season on its masts, and {X_pronoun} would make the colony's on its {TALE}, at the Line's price: for a trader of goods or of arms, for hands, or a good word with a people the colony stands poorly with. A call on the radio is answered within hours.

[runner] {X_nameDef}, a lineman of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. The colony has no radio, so the Line sends its calls by runner, one a season. {X_pronoun} would carry this season's for the colony, at the Line's price: for a trader of goods or of arms, for hands, or a good word with a people the colony stands poorly with. It would be answered in a day or two.

[age0] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has run to the gate. The Line passes one call a season along its hilltops for each place, and the colony's is free to give, at the Line's price: a trader of goods or of arms, hands, or a good word with a people the colony stands poorly with.

[age1] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a satchel of signal flags. One call a season goes down the Line's towers for each place, and {X_pronoun} would send the colony's, at the Line's price: a trader of goods or of arms, hands, or a good word with a people the colony stands poorly with.

[age2] {X_nameDef}, an operator of {FACTION} in a signal-orange coat, has come up the road. The Line gives each place one call a season on its masts, and {X_pronoun} would make the colony's, at the Line's price: a trader of goods or of arms, hands, or a good word with a people the colony stands poorly with.

[age3] {X_nameDef}, an operator of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a handset on a strap. One call a season goes out on the Line's relays for each place, and {X_pronoun} would make the colony's, at the Line's price: a trader of goods or of arms, hands, or a good word with a people the colony stands poorly with.

li.label: Call for a trader of goods ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} will make the call, and a caravan with goods to sell will come.

li.label: Call for a trader of arms ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} will make the call, and a caravan with weapons and armour to sell will come.

li.label: Call for hands ({DEAD} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} will put out word that the colony takes in people, and someone looking for a place will come to join.

li.label: Have them speak well of us to {ENEMY} ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} will see that the Line speaks well of the colony to {ENEMY}.

li.label: Not this season
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods and goes back to the road.

lines.li: [call] I'll put it out on the line.
[later] Then the call is saved for someone else.
[called] It's on the line, they'll answer.
[off] I'll have it at the next mast by nightfall.

IncidentDef.label: a mast at a friend's town

titles.li: A mast at a friend's town

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a lineman of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. The Line knows the colony writes to {RELATION} at {PLACE}. For {COUNT} silver, or {TALE} components, it would raise a mast at {PLACE}, and the colony's letters there and the answers would take half the days.

[mast] {X_nameDef}, a lineman of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. The colony's own mast already carries its letters, and {X_pronoun} offers a second at {PLACE}, where {RELATION} lives, for {COUNT} silver or {TALE} components. With a mast at each end, the letters would still take half the days, but they would go the Line's way the whole road.

[age0] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate. The Line would put up a signal post on the hill above {PLACE}, where {RELATION} lives, for {COUNT} silver or {TALE} components, and the colony's messages there and back would be passed along by signal in half the days.

[age1] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a coil of rope and a bundle of flags. For {COUNT} silver, or {TALE} components, the Line would raise a flag-and-lamp tower at {PLACE}, where {RELATION} lives, and the colony's letters there and back would take half the days.

[age2] {X_nameDef}, a lineman of {FACTION} in a signal-orange oilskin, has come to the gate. For {COUNT} silver, or {TALE} components, the Line would raise a mast at {PLACE}, where {RELATION} lives, and the colony's letters there and back would go by wire, in half the days.

[age3] {X_nameDef}, a lineman of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a relay kit. For {COUNT} silver, or {TALE} components, the Line would set up a relay at {PLACE}, where {RELATION} lives, and the colony's letters there and back would take half the days.

li.label: Pay {COUNT} silver for the mast
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} takes the silver and sets off for {PLACE} to raise the mast.

li.label: Pay in components ({TALE})
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} takes the components and sets off for {PLACE} to raise the mast.

li.label: Not now
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods and goes back to the road.

lines.li: [raise] I'll go on to {PLACE} and raise it there.
[later] The offer stands if you change your mind.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a lineman of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. A crew of the Line would camp a week on {PLACE} and raise a {TALE} there while they string wire through the district. While it stands the colony's letters could go out by their wire, and at night their radio carries the region's news.

[mast,nomast] {X_nameDef}, a lineman of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. A crew would camp a week on {PLACE} and raise a {TALE} there while they work the wire. The colony has no mast of its own, and {X_pronoun} says the crew might sell it theirs when they go, for a fee.

[tower] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate. A crew of the Line would camp a week on {PLACE} and put up a {TALE}, and from it read the next tower's flags and lamps. While it stands the colony's letters could be passed along by signal.

[age0] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked to the gate. Three or four of the Line's people would camp a week on {PLACE} and put up a {TALE} there, to pass signals along the hills. The colony's messages could go with theirs while they stay.

[age1] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a bundle of signal flags. A crew would camp a week on {PLACE} and raise a {TALE}, and the colony's letters could go along the line of towers with theirs while it stands.

[age2] {X_nameDef}, a lineman of {FACTION} in a signal-orange oilskin, has come to the gate. A crew would camp a week on {PLACE} and raise a {TALE} while they string wire. The colony's letters could go out by their wire, and their radio plays the region's news at night.

[age3] {X_nameDef}, a lineman of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. A crew would camp a week on {PLACE} and set up a {TALE} while they lay new line, and the colony's letters could go out on it while it stands.

li.label: Let them camp and raise it
li.outcome: The line crew will come up to {PLACE} and make camp.

li.label: Let them camp, and send food with them for the week (10 meals)
li.outcome: Ten meals are carried out to {X_nameDef}, and the line crew will come up to {PLACE} and make camp.

li.label: Not this time
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods and goes back to the road.

lines.li: [camp] We'll be up there by nightfall.
[later] Then we'll camp further down the line.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a miner of {FACTION}, has run to the gate. The pit at {PLACE} has caved in with miners below, and the union is digging for them. {X_pronoun} asks for {A_nameDef}, the colony's best miner, for {COUNT} days of shifts at the face, for the union's pay of {DEAD} silver.

[doctor] {X_nameDef}, a miner of {FACTION}, has run to the gate. The pit at {PLACE} has caved in with miners below. The union asks for {A_nameDef}, the colony's best miner, and {B_nameDef}, its doctor, for {COUNT} days: {A_nameDef} to dig at the face and {B_nameDef} to see to the ones they bring up. The union pays {DEAD} silver each.

[age0] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come running to the gate. The diggings at {PLACE} have fallen in on the people working them. {X_pronoun} asks for {A_nameDef}, who digs best of the colony, for {COUNT} days of digging, for {DEAD} silver.

[age1] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate covered in dust. The shaft at {PLACE} has caved in with miners below, and the union needs every pick it can get. {X_pronoun} asks for {A_nameDef} for {COUNT} days, for {DEAD} silver.

[age2] {X_nameDef}, a miner of {FACTION} in a red armband, has run up the road. The pit at {PLACE} has caved in and men are trapped below the second level. The union asks for {A_nameDef} for {COUNT} days of shifts, for {DEAD} silver.

[age3] {X_nameDef}, a miner of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. A shaft at {PLACE} has collapsed and the union's diggers can't reach the crew below fast enough. {X_pronoun} asks for {A_nameDef} for {COUNT} days, for {DEAD} silver.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} pack for the road and set out for {PLACE}.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} alone
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} packs for the road and sets out for {PLACE}.

li.label: We can't spare anyone
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} turns and runs back the way {X_pronoun} came.

lines.li: [sent] Thank you, the union won't forget it.
[later] Then we dig with what we have.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an assayer of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a driller. The union has found oil under the colony's ground, {PLACE}. They would sink a {THING} there for the colony, for {COUNT} silver, or for a year's share: {TALE} chemfuel a season for four seasons.

[age1] {X_nameDef}, an assayer of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a driller and a cart of pipe. There is oil under the colony's ground {PLACE}, {X_pronoun} says, and the union would sink a {THING} there, for {COUNT} silver or a year's share of {TALE} chemfuel a season.

[age2] {X_nameDef}, an assayer of {FACTION} in a red armband, has come up the road with a driller and a rig on a cart. The union has found oil {PLACE}, and would sink a {THING} for the colony, for {COUNT} silver or a year's share of {TALE} chemfuel a season.

[age3] {X_nameDef}, an assayer of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a driller and a survey drone. The scans show oil {PLACE}, and the union would sink a {THING} for the colony, for {COUNT} silver or a year's share of {TALE} chemfuel a season.

[age0] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a driller. They have found where the black oil lies under the colony's ground, {PLACE}, and would sink a {THING} there for {COUNT} silver, or for a share of {TALE} chemfuel a season for a year.

li.label: Have them sink the well ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and the driller go out {PLACE} and start drilling.

li.label: the union's price for the well
Have them sink the well for a year's share
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and the driller go out {PLACE} and start drilling. The union will collect {TALE} chemfuel a season for a year.

li.label: Leave the oil where it is
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shrugs and goes back to the road.

lines.li: [sink] We'll have it flowing by tonight.
[later] It'll still be there if you change your mind.
[done] There, the well is yours.

IncidentDef.label: a seam marked for the drill

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an assayer of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. Deep under the colony's ground {PLACE} there is a seam of {THING}, about {TALE} of it. For {COUNT} silver {X_pronoun} would mark it, and the union's drill crew would come for it the day after.

[scanned] {X_nameDef}, an assayer of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. The colony's own scanner has shown the deep ground, and {X_pronoun} has worked out where the best of it lies: {TALE} of {THING}, {PLACE}. For {COUNT} silver {X_pronoun} would mark it for the union's drill.

[age0] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a bag of rock samples. There is {THING} deep under the colony's ground {PLACE}, about {TALE} of it, and for {COUNT} silver {X_pronoun} would mark the spot for the union's diggers.

[age1] {X_nameDef}, an assayer of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a pick and a sample bag. Deep under the ground {PLACE} lies a seam of {THING}, some {TALE}, and for {COUNT} silver {X_pronoun} would stake it for the union's drill.

[age2] {X_nameDef}, an assayer of {FACTION} in a red armband, has come up the road. {X_pronoun} has tested the ground {PLACE} and found a deep seam of {THING}, about {TALE}. For {COUNT} silver {X_pronoun} would mark it, and the union's drill crew would come for it.

[age3] {X_nameDef}, an assayer of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a ground scanner. There is a deep seam of {THING} {PLACE}, about {TALE}, and for {COUNT} silver {X_pronoun} would mark it for the union's drill.

li.label: Have {X_objective} mark it ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes out {PLACE} to mark the seam.

li.label: Have {X_objective} mark it, and send {A_nameDef} to walk the ground with {X_objective} ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes out {PLACE} to mark the seam, and {A_nameDef} goes with {X_objective} to learn how the ground is read.

li.label: Not now
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shrugs and goes back to the road.

lines.li: [mark] I'll show you where it lies.
[later] It'll keep, seams don't go anywhere.
[marked] It's under here, the crew will come for it.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a shift-captain of {FACTION}, has come to the gate at dusk. {X_pronoun} has heard the colony's people are worn down by {TALE}, and asks to speak at the colony's fire tonight about how the union keeps its shifts.

[longhours] {X_nameDef}, a shift-captain of {FACTION}, has come to the gate at dusk. The colony is working long hours, {X_pronoun} says, and it shows on its people's faces. {X_pronoun} asks to speak at the fire tonight about how the union keeps its shifts.

[striking] {X_nameDef}, a shift-captain of {FACTION}, has come to the gate at dusk, on the road while the union is on strike. {X_pronoun} has heard the colony's people are worn down by {TALE}, and asks to speak at its fire tonight about the union's shifts.

[age0] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate as the light goes. The colony's people look tired, {X_pronoun} says, and {X_pronoun} would like to sit at their fire tonight and tell them how the union shares out its work.

[age1] {X_nameDef}, a shift-captain of {FACTION}, has come to the gate at dusk with a lantern. {X_pronoun} has heard the colony's people are worn down by {TALE}, and asks to speak at their fire about the union's rule that everyone comes up at the end of the shift.

[age2] {X_nameDef}, a shift-captain of {FACTION} in a red armband, has come up the road at dusk. {X_pronoun} has heard the colony's people are worn down by {TALE}, and asks to speak at the fire tonight about how the union keeps its shifts and its days off.

[age3] {X_nameDef}, a shift-captain of {FACTION}, has come to the gate at dusk. The colony's people are worn down by {TALE}, {X_pronoun} has heard, and {X_pronoun} asks to speak at the fire tonight about how the union keeps its rota.

li.label: Let {X_objective} speak at the fire tonight
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} will speak at the colony's fire this evening, to whoever comes.

lines.li: Everyone comes up at the end of the shift.
A tired hand is how people get hurt.
The union puts it to a vote, and so could you.
One day in seven, nobody goes down the pit.

li.label: Let {X_objective} speak, and give {X_objective} supper
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is given supper, and speaks at the colony's fire this evening, to whoever comes.

lines.li: Everyone comes up at the end of the shift.
A tired hand is how people get hurt.
The union puts it to a vote, and so could you.
One day in seven, nobody goes down the pit.

li.label: Not tonight
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods and goes back to the road.

lines.li: [speak] I'll keep it short, they need their sleep.
[later] Then look after them yourselves.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a shift-captain of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. The union at {PLACE} has voted to strike, and some of the strikers would keep a picket by the colony's road while it lasts: a camp with a fire, on the road the union's trade uses.

[age0] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate. The union's diggers at {PLACE} have put down their picks together, and a few of them would camp by the colony's road until it is settled, with a fire and their songs.

[age1] {X_nameDef}, a shift-captain of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. The union at {PLACE} has voted to walk out, and some of the strikers would keep a picket by the colony's road until it is over, a fire going day and night.

[age2] {X_nameDef}, a shift-captain of {FACTION} in a red armband, has come up the road. The union at {PLACE} has voted to strike, and some of the strikers would keep a picket by the colony's road while it lasts, with a fire and their songs in the evening.

[age3] {X_nameDef}, a shift-captain of {FACTION}, has come to the gate. The union at {PLACE} has voted to stop work, and some of the strikers would keep a picket by the colony's road until it is settled.

li.label: Let them keep the picket
li.outcome: The strikers will come and make camp by the colony's road.

li.label: Let them keep it, and send wood for their fire ({TALE} wood)
li.outcome: Wood is carried out to {X_nameDef}, and the strikers will come and make camp by the colony's road.

li.label: No picket here
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods and goes back to the road.

lines.li: [camp] We'll keep it peaceful, you have the union's word.
[later] Then we picket somewhere else.
